doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: What makes a great ballad: Hodges, Nance, Lawson
summary: Listening to Johnny Hodges, Ray Nance and Yank Lawson shaped his ballad playing.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Is there a specific art to playing a ballad? What goes into playing a great ballad on the keyboard?

I don’t know. Well I think you have to listen to records a lot. You know I was influenced by people like Johnny Hodges. I immediately think when you mention that I think of Johnny Hodges of Duke Ellington’s band you know. And people like that. Yank Lawson, the trumpet player who just passed away a year ago. Certain musicians that I really think were — really had — almost made you cry when they play a ballad you know. Oh, the violinist, Ray Nance with Duke Ellington. I was crazy about Duke Ellington as you can tell. Certain people I think just — I think that inspiration helped me a lot. And you have to see them in person, too, which I have seen them a lot.
Seeing a great artist in person is different from just getting the record, isn’t it?
Yeah. Particularly Johnny Hodges. He was a miracle man as far as I am concerned.
